subject: Producing sigma visuals from a distributional model

messages.author: 019b63fbe417066b
messages.subject: Producing sigma visuals from a distributional model
parts:
Hey Paul, I was wondering if I could answer a question I have about Brms. I've been experimenting with distributional models in Brms, and I was wondering if you could help with obtaining the sigma visuals. I've noticed when i use marginal_effects plot on my model, I get the mean effects twice, and not the sigmas. My question is, do i need to do anything in particular to get the visuals for both the mean and residual standard deviations. Also, wanted to say thank you for producing a spectacular r package! and i attached the code below as an example.

RelativeBayesStrengthFULLnoDistribution<-brm( bf(ABSRelativeStrengthDistance ~ s(AgeActual.s, by=Group) + mean.ndvi.s+(1+AgeActual.s|2|IDJuve),sigma ~ s(AgeActual.s, by=Group) + mean.ndvi.s + (1+AgeActual.s|2|IDJuve)),autocor = cor_ar(p=1,formula = ~AgeSeq|IDJuve),data =RelativeFinalDataSet,iter=1000,chains = 4,cores = 4, family = gaussian,prior = set_prior("normal(0,10)"))

Cheers

Jonathan

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Producing sigma visuals from a distributional model
parts:
Try out

marginal_effects(RelativeBayesStrengthFULLnoDistribution, dpar = "sigma")

See ?fitted.brmsfit for more help.

I am wondering though, why you get the (same?) mean effects twice. Which version of brms are you using?
